question: A 56 year old female comes to the ED complaining of moderate right eye pain, headache, and acute onset of blurry vision, which she describes as colored halos around lights. She was watching a movie at home with her husband about an hour ago when the pain began. On physical exam of her right eye, her pupil is mid-dilated and unresponsive to light. Her right eyeball is firm to pressure. Intraocular pressure (IOP) measured with tonometer is elevated at 36mmHg. Which of the following is the most appropriate emergency treatment?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Acute angle-closure glaucoma -> increased intraocular pressure -> 36mmHg -> 95% CHAIN: Elevated IOP -> optic nerve damage risk -> vision loss -> 90% CHAIN: Mid-dilated pupil -> unresponsive to light -> 95% CHAIN: Colored halos around lights -> acute angle-closure glaucoma symptom -> 90% CHAIN: Firm eyeball to pressure -> 95% CHAIN: Timolol ophthalmic solution -> reduce intraocular pressure -> 95% CHAIN: Laser peripheral iridotomy -> definitive treatment for acute angle-closure glaucoma -> 95%
enhanced_information: The most appropriate emergency treatment for acute angle-closure glaucoma with elevated intraocular pressure, mid-dilated pupil, and colored halos around lights is laser peripheral iridotomy, which is the definitive treatment for this condition.
analysis: The patient presents with symptoms and signs consistent with acute angle-closure glaucoma, including elevated intraocular pressure, mid-dilated pupil, and colored halos around lights. The definitive treatment for acute angle-closure glaucoma is laser peripheral iridotomy, which helps to relieve the blockage causing the increased intraocular pressure. Timolol, epinephrine, anti-cholinergic, and NSAID ophthalmic solutions are not the primary treatments for acute angle-closure glaucoma and would not address the underlying cause of the symptoms. Laser peripheral iridotomy is the most appropriate emergency treatment in this scenario.
